A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The full text, tables, equations, figures and Appendix A support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of parallel encoding, attention entropy, attention sinks and selective attention across language modeling, ICL, RAG and synthetic recall tasks, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds context-length results and a finer breakdown of the selective-attention ablation.

M1.justification: Parallel encoding, shared attention sinks and Algorithm 1's selective-attention procedure are unchanged, including scoring, selection, aggregation and renormalization. The added explanations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same language-modeling, ICL, RAG and synthetic-recall datasets and tasks. The added appendix plots reuse this coverage at different context lengths.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain full attention, naive parallel encoding, sink/selection variants and the oracle-key control. The newly cited related works are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: V2 Figures 10–11 extend the reported sink/selection comparison from 8K to 4K and 16K sequences. Those lengths already appeared in the naive-parallel evaluation; existing metrics, decoding, models and parallel-degree settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds context-length checks of the entropy-reduction methods and a TREC-coarse breakdown of the top-K ablation in Section 4.3.1, footnote 10. The original aggregation and oracle-key analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing averaging practices and the reported entropy–performance correlation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and all retained plotted results are unchanged. V2 adds 4K/16K entropy-reduction curves and reports TREC-coarse accuracy of 0.45 for K=1 versus 0.48 for K=5 in footnote 10.

T1.justification: New Section 2.1 states the standard entropy formula for the metric already used in v1. The operation-count derivation and existing mathematical reasoning are unchanged; no new formal result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: naive parallel encoding degrades performance, elevated attention entropy correlates with degradation, and sinks and selective attention mitigate the gaps without fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds an interpretation connecting diffuse attention with broader contextual understanding and concentrated attention with precise retrieval. Footnote 9 adds a qualitative, unmeasured claim of slight selection overhead without layer aggregation. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompts, top-5 scoring, default K=2, aggregation rules and the two-pass requirement are retained. The new overhead footnote restates the existing per-layer procedure rather than supplying a new implementation setting or resource-access disclosure.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Wang et al. (2024) on precision-related benefits of sink tokens and Attanasio et al. (2022) on entropy regularization for bias mitigation. These modestly broaden the related-work discussion without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: V2 renames Section 2, inserts an attention-entropy subsection, expands captions and adds explanatory footnotes and related-work sentences. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds two multi-panel appendix figures and expands the Figure 1 and Table 1 captions. Table 2 moves to page 8, and the original Figures 10–11 become Figures 12–13. Existing graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added 4K/16K results and TREC-coarse ablation detail modestly strengthen empirical support, while Section 2.1 and expanded captions improve clarity. These gains preserve the original evidence and claims. They do not resolve the acknowledged absence of measured efficiency or the remaining performance gaps; the new slight-overhead assertion is still unmeasured.
